title: About page
content:
Twenty years of watching students decide they're "not a science person".

They almost always are. SMARTin SCIENCE exists to prove it — in four weeks.

Rod Martin

Expert Science Tutor · Former Head of Science

  • Over 20 years of teaching experience
  • Former Head of Science in a UK secondary school
  • Biology, Chemistry and Physics to GCSE level
  • GCSE Sciences specialist for Y9-Y11
  • Whole-department experience of how papers are marked
  • Sessions built around confidence, not just content

From the front of the classroom

Rod Martin has spent over twenty years teaching science in UK schools, including running an entire science department as Head of Science. In that time, he has taught every part of the Science specifications to every kind of student — the ones who love it, the ones who dread it, and the very large group in between who simply lost the thread somewhere in Year 9.

That last group is the reason SMARTin SCIENCE exists.

Twenty years of it

  • 20+ years of science teaching experience
  • Continues to achieve above national pass rates in science
  • Regularly standardises and moderates science exam papers — so knows what answers are expected
  • Teaches all the GCSE science curriculums (Combined Science, Biology, Chemistry and Physics) to Higher tier
  • 7 years in charge of a large science department — first as Head of Science, then as Assistant Headteacher in charge of science & data
  • Former Lead Practitioner for Teaching and Learning — has guided and supported newly qualified teachers into the profession

Why four weeks

Long tutoring arrangements can drift. A fixed four-week course does not. Each week has one job — Biology, Chemistry, Physics, then exam technique — and every session ends with the student able to name something they can now do that they couldn't do an hour earlier.

Four weeks is also long enough to change habits: how to read a command word, how to structure a six-mark answer, how to rearrange an equation without panicking. Those habits carry into every paper afterwards, which is why the effect outlasts the course.

Knowing where the marks actually go

Having taught the specification and led a department, Rod knows exactly where students lose marks — and it is rarely where parents assume. It's the "explain" answered as a "describe". The unit left off. The graph not fully annotated. The six-marker that contains all the right science in no usable order.

These are fixable in weeks, not years. That's what week four is for.

The three values behind every session

  • Empowerment — students leave able to do the thing themselves, not just watch it be done.
  • Engagement — if a session is boring, it isn't working. Activities, comparisons and real examples do the heavy lifting.
  • Excellence — high expectations, clearly explained, with the support to actually meet them.

Leeds in person, England and Wales online

In-person sessions run across Leeds. Everywhere else in England and Wales, the same course runs online — same worksheets, same homework, same feedback.
